A plant stem is measured to be 16.0 cm, correct to one decimal place.

A measurement correct to one decimal place has an absolute error (precision) of half the unit of measurement:

$$\begin{aligned} \text{percentage error} &= \dfrac{0.05}{16.0}\times 100\% \\ &= 0.3125\% \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
The average energy used in kilojoules per kilogram of body mass by a basketball player in a leisure game is 11.98 kJ/kg per 30 minutes of play. Joshua who weighs 70 kg, drinks a soft drink that contains 162 kilocalories. Joshua is to play a basketball game with his friends.

For approximately how long he should play in order to burn off the energy contained in the drink given that 1 kilocalorie $= 4.184$ kJ?
parts.note: Food energy in kilojoules and kilocalories is not in the 2024 course.

solutions.latex:
First convert the energy in the drink to kilojoules, using $1 \text{ kcal} = 4.184 \text{ kJ}$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{energy} &= 162 \times 4.184 \\ &= 677.808 \text{ kJ} \end{aligned}$$
Next find the energy Joshua uses in $30$ minutes of play, using $11.98$ kJ/kg per $30$ minutes and a mass of $70$ kg.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{energy used} &= 11.98 \times 70 \\ &= 838.6 \text{ kJ per 30 minutes} \end{aligned}$$
The time needed is the fraction of $30$ minutes required to use $677.808$ kJ.
$$\begin{aligned} t &= \dfrac{677.808}{838.6}\times 30 \\ &\approx 24.2 \text{ minutes} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{approximately 24 minutes (option B)}$$

Add the two parts.

parts.note: Student must form the quadratic A = x(8-x) from a description and find its maximum

solutions.latex:
The area of a right triangle is $\dfrac{1}{2}\times\text{base}\times\text{height}$.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times 2x\times(8-x) \\ &= 8x-x^2 \end{aligned}$$
Differentiate to find the stationary point.
$$\dfrac{dA}{dx}=8-2x=0 \quad\text{so}\quad x=4$$
Since $\dfrac{d^2A}{dx^2}=-2<0$, this is a maximum.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 8(4)-4^2 \\ &= 16 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex:
At a schools swimming carnival, the finish times for students under 17 who competed in the 50 m backstroke race are found to be normally distributed with a mean race time of 42 seconds and a standard deviation of 3 seconds.

The standard normal distribution table is shown. The values in the table represent the area under the normal curve to the left of the $z$-score.

\exfigure{250_q33_1}

Using standardised scores and the standard normal distribution table, find the probability that a randomly chosen competitor achieves a finish time between 43 and 46 seconds. Give your answer correct to three decimal places.
parts.note: Normal probabilities from a standard normal (z) table.

solutions.latex:
Standardise each time using $z=\dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$ with $\mu=42$ and $\sigma=3$.
$$\begin{aligned} z_{43} &= \dfrac{43-42}{3} \approx 0.33 \\ z_{46} &= \dfrac{46-42}{3} \approx 1.33 \end{aligned}$$
From the table, the area to the left of $z=0.33$ is $0.62930$ and the area to the left of $z=1.33$ is $0.90824$.
$$\begin{aligned} P(43<X<46) &= P(z<1.33)-P(z<0.33) \\ &= 0.90824-0.62930 \\ &= 0.27894 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ P(43<X<46) \approx 0.279$$

Hector’s height is measured as 1.88 metres, correct to two decimal places.

Between what two measurements would his actual height lie?
parts.note: Limits of accuracy of a measurement is old syllabus (measurement error).

solutions.latex:
Correct to two decimal places means rounded to the nearest $0.01$ m.

The possible error is half a unit of the last place: $\dfrac{0.01}{2} = 0.005$ m.

So the actual height lies between $1.88 - 0.005$ and $1.88 + 0.005$:
$$1.875 \text{ m} \text{ and } 1.885 \text{ m}$$
This matches option B.

solutions.latex:
Both triangles have a right angle, since the pole and the post are vertical and the ground is level. They also share the same angle $\alpha^\circ$, since the sun's rays are parallel. Two angles are equal, so the third angles are equal too.

$\therefore$ the triangles are equiangular, hence similar.

Corresponding sides of similar triangles are in the same ratio: height over shadow length.
$$\dfrac{h}{6.3}=\dfrac{1.6}{1.4}$$
$$\begin{aligned} h &= \dfrac{1.6}{1.4}\times 6.3 \\ &= 7.2 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ h=7.2 \text{ m}$$

7538.stem: Alex weighs 75 kg. When participating in a marathon, Alex's body typically uses 12 kJ per 1 kg of his body mass for an hour of running. He completed his last marathon in four and a half hours.

parts.latex: How many kilojoules of energy did his body use in completing the marathon?
parts.note: Body and food energy in kilojoules is not in the 2024 course.

parts.latex:
The body is only about $25\%$ efficient in converting food to usable energy.

If a kilogram of pasta contains 3000 kJ of energy, how many kilograms of pasta would Alex need to consume to give him the energy to complete the marathon.
parts.note: Food energy in kilojoules (pasta kJ content, body efficiency) is not in the 2024 course.

solutions.latex:
Energy used is the rate per kilogram times mass times time.
$$12\times75\times4.5=4050\text{ kJ}$$

meta.source_flag: Source working for (a) reads $\dfrac{250}{1000}\times4.5=1.125\text{ kW}$, which does not answer the question; I replaced it with $12\times75\times4.5=4050$ kJ. Part (b) uses 1.125 kW$\times 3600$ = 4050 kJ, so the values are consistent.

solutions.latex:
The body is $25\%$ efficient, so the food energy needed is four times the energy used.
$$25\%\text{ of food energy}=4050\text{ kJ (from part (a))}$$
$$\begin{aligned} 100\%\text{ of food energy}&=4050\times4 \\ &=16\,200\text{ kJ} \end{aligned}$$
Pasta needed:
$$\begin{aligned} 16\,200\div3000&=5.4\text{ kg} \end{aligned}$$
